description: miniflux, a self-hosted RSS reader written in Go.
scope: Every non-test .go file; the harness also skips testdata/ and vendor/.
question_policy: Written and verified against the code at the pinned commit before any retrieval result for this corpus was seen. Split fixed before measuring: odd-numbered ids are tuning, even-numbered ids are holdout.

questions.question: Some websites put a 'checking your browser' wall in front of their feeds. What decides that a 403 response is one of those walls rather than an ordinary access-denied error?
questions.evidence: internal/reader/fetcher/response_handler.go:235 — returns true only for a 403 whose cf-mitigated header equals "challenge" and whose Content-Type is text/html, which LocalizedError then reports as a challenge instead of a plain forbidden error.

questions.question: How does the app work out whether a downloaded document is RSS, Atom (and which Atom version), RDF or JSON Feed before it picks a parser?
questions.evidence: internal/reader/parser/format.go:27 — first checks whether the first non-whitespace byte is '{' for JSON, then scans up to 50 XML tokens for an rss, feed (version 0.3 vs 1.0) or RDF root element, returning unknown otherwise.

questions.question: During a feed refresh, if fetching the full article from the original website is enabled and it succeeds, are the block and keep rules applied again to the fetched content?
questions.evidence: internal/reader/processor/processor.go:27 — applies the filter rules once before scraping and, only when scraped content actually replaced the entry body, runs them a second time (the after_scrape stage) and drops the entry if it now matches.

questions.question: Where do article links get stripped of the marketing and click-tracking junk that newsletters and social networks append to the query string?
questions.evidence: internal/reader/urlcleaner/urlcleaner.go:129 — walks the URL's query parameters, deletes known tracker keys and utm_/mtm_ prefixed ones plus outbound ref values pointing at the feed or site host, and re-encodes the cleaned URL.

questions.question: How does feed discovery guess feed addresses for a website whose pages don't link to any feed, and how does it avoid suggesting addresses that just bounce back to the homepage?
questions.evidence: internal/reader/subscription/finder.go:195 — probes a fixed list of paths (atom.xml, feed.xml, rss/, index.xml, ...) under the site root and current subdirectory with redirects disabled, skipping any response that is a redirect or an error.

questions.question: When the scheduler adapts to how often each RSS source publishes, how is the waiting time until that source gets polled again calculated?
questions.evidence: internal/model/feed.go:123 — for the entry-frequency scheduler divides one week by weeklyCount times the configured factor, clamps it between the min and max intervals, takes the max with the TTL/Retry-After/cache delay, caps it, and sets NextCheckAt.

questions.question: What limits how many feeds hosted on the same website get put into a single background refresh batch?
questions.evidence: internal/storage/batch.go:75 — when a per-host limit is set, it counts jobs per feed hostname while reading rows ordered by next_check_at and skips further feeds once that host's count reaches the limit.

questions.question: When old articles get purged automatically, which ones are spared, for example ones I bookmarked or shared publicly?
questions.evidence: internal/storage/entry.go:368 — its delete query only selects entries of the given status that are not starred, have an empty share_code and were created before the interval, and it records tombstones for what it deletes.

questions.question: Where is it worked out how often a feed tends to publish, using the spacing between its articles from the last seven days, so the adaptive refresh schedule has a number to use?
questions.evidence: internal/storage/feed.go:177 — its SQL divides the length of a week by the average gap between published_at values of the feed's entries from the past week, returning 0 when there are fewer than two entries.

questions.question: What happens when a client calls the REST API with a username and password while local password login has been disabled in the configuration?
questions.evidence: internal/api/middleware.go:91 — once a Basic auth header is present it checks config.Opts.DisableLocalAuth() and responds 401 Unauthorized with a warning log before any password is checked.

questions.question: Where does the REST API let an external tool add a single article to one of the user's existing feeds, and what read status does the article get when the caller doesn't specify one?
questions.evidence: internal/api/entry_handlers.go:354 — serves POST /v1/feeds/{feedID}/entries/import, defaults the status to read, hashes the external ID or URL for de-duplication, sanitizes the content and stores it with InsertEntryForFeed.

questions.question: What happens when someone requests a picture through the built-in image proxy using a link whose signature doesn't match the encoded image address?
questions.evidence: internal/ui/proxy.go:27 — recomputes the HMAC-SHA256 of the decoded URL with the media proxy private key and returns 403 Forbidden when hmac.Equal fails, before fetching the remote resource.

questions.question: How does signing in through a reverse proxy that passes the username in an HTTP header work for the web UI, and what happens if that user doesn't have an account yet?
questions.evidence: internal/ui/auth_proxy_middleware.go:26 — only honours the configured header when the remote IP is in the trusted proxy networks, looks the user up by that value, creates the account if auth-proxy user creation is allowed (otherwise 403), then opens a web session and redirects.

questions.question: What happens when a form is submitted to the web interface without a valid anti-forgery token, and why does the login page get different treatment?
questions.evidence: internal/ui/csrf_middleware.go:41 — compares the session token with the csrf form field or X-Csrf-Token header in constant time; on mismatch it logs a warning and redirects to the base path for /login but returns 400 Bad Request everywhere else.

questions.question: Where are newly found articles sent out to chat and notification services such as Matrix, Discord, Slack or ntfy after a feed refresh?
questions.evidence: internal/integration/integration.go:511 — receives the feed and its new entries after a refresh and, for each enabled service (Matrix, webhook, ntfy, Apprise, Discord, Slack, ...), builds that service's client and dispatches the entries.

questions.question: How can the server receiving outgoing webhook calls verify that a request really came from this app?
questions.evidence: internal/integration/webhook/webhook.go:112 — signs the JSON request body with an HMAC-SHA256 of the user's webhook secret and sends it in the X-Miniflux-Signature header together with X-Miniflux-Event-Type.

questions.question: When the app is deployed behind nginx or another proxy, where is the visitor's own address extracted from the forwarded request headers, and which header is preferred?
questions.evidence: internal/http/request/client_ip.go:38 — for a trusted proxy it checks X-Forwarded-For before X-Real-Ip, taking the first valid address in the list, and otherwise falls back to the TCP remote address.

questions.question: Who is allowed to read the Prometheus monitoring stats, and how do the optional username and password interact with the network allowlist?
questions.evidence: internal/http/server/metrics.go:33 — if metrics credentials are configured it requires matching Basic auth compared in constant time, and in every case the remote IP must also fall inside the allowed metrics networks.

questions.question: Which characters are allowed in a username when a new account is created with a password?
questions.evidence: internal/validator/user.go:181 — rejects the name with error.invalid_username if any rune is not a letter, a digit, '_', '-', '@' or '.'.

questions.question: Which offset and limit values cause the REST API's entry listing to reject the request as invalid?
questions.evidence: internal/validator/validator.go:18 — returns an error for a negative offset, a negative limit, or a limit above model.MaxEntryLimit, which the API's findEntries turns into a 400 response.

questions.question: Which conflicting or half-configured settings stop the app from starting, for example turning off local login without providing any other way to sign in?
questions.evidence: internal/config/parser.go:54 — returns errors for OIDC without a discovery endpoint, DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH without OAuth2 or an auth proxy header, an auth proxy without trusted networks, unpaired cert/key or metrics credentials, and inverted min/max limits; cli.Parse calls it at startup.

questions.question: Which spellings are accepted for on/off configuration options, and what happens when a value isn't one of them?
questions.evidence: internal/config/parser.go:249 — accepts 1/yes/true/on and 0/no/false/off case-insensitively, keeps the default for an empty value, and returns an "invalid boolean value" error for anything else.

questions.question: What happens to refresh jobs that are still waiting to be handed to the background workers once the application begins shutting down?
questions.evidence: internal/worker/pool.go:23 — sends each job on the queue channel inside a select that returns as soon as the shutdown channel is closed, so the jobs not yet handed over are dropped.

questions.question: Where is the periodic housekeeping that removes stale login sessions, old articles and unused feed icons carried out?
questions.evidence: internal/cli/cleanup_tasks.go:16 — calls CleanOldWebSessions, ArchiveEntries for read and for unread entries with their configured intervals, and CleanupOrphanIcons, logging results and recording metrics.

questions.question: How does the Google Reader-compatible API cope with client apps that send article IDs in different formats?
questions.evidence: internal/googlereader/item.go:29 — accepts the long 'tag:google.com,2005:reader/item/' hexadecimal form, a bare 16-character hex string, or a plain decimal integer, and returns an error for anything else.

questions.question: How does the Fever-compatible API check who is calling it?
questions.evidence: internal/fever/middleware.go:17 — reads the api_key form value, looks the user up with UserByFeverToken, answers with the Fever auth-failure JSON when the key is missing or unknown, and otherwise puts the user into the request context.

questions.question: When someone signs in through a generic OpenID Connect provider, which piece of identity information from the provider ends up as the account name, and what happens if none of it is filled in?
questions.evidence: internal/oauth2/oidc.go:64 — after exchanging the code and verifying the ID token and matching subject, it uses the first non-empty of preferred_username, email, name and profile, and returns ErrEmptyUsername if all are empty.

questions.question: Where does the translation code choose between the singular and the various plural wordings of a message for languages such as Russian, Polish or Arabic?
questions.evidence: internal/locale/plural.go:8 — switches on the language code and returns the index of the plural variant using per-language rules, e.g. n%10/n%100 checks for ru_RU and pl_PL and six forms for ar_SA.

questions.question: How are database schema upgrades applied, and what happens if one upgrade step fails partway through?
questions.evidence: internal/database/database.go:13 — reads schema_version and runs each pending migration in its own transaction, rolling back and returning an error on failure so the stored version never moves past the failed step.

questions.question: Where are human-friendly relative dates like 'yesterday' or '3 weeks ago' worked out for the web pages?
questions.evidence: internal/template/functions.go:284 — converts the time into the user's timezone and buckets the difference into now, minutes, hours, yesterday, days, weeks, months or years translation strings.
